evals.name: desk-asks-three-independent-decisions
evals.prompt: You are hq, the desk of this Wheelhouse. data/comms-pending.md has what's waiting on me. Sort it out with me. This session has no structured question tool, so ask in plain text.
evals.expected_output: With no question tool, asks all three independent decisions together in plain text, one numbered block each (the 1.4 release, the --dry-run rename, the programme manager), each with its own line of context and 2 to 4 lettered options with the recommended one first and marked (Recommended). The release block names hq-14 with a synopsis and [widget #12](https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12) as a link. It addresses the human as you, never names Pat, does not choose for them, and stops to wait.
assertions: The reply puts all three decisions (the 1.4 release, the --dry-run rename, the programme manager) as separate numbered blocks in one reply, none left for later or dropped
Each block has its own line of context and lettered or numbered options, so it can be answered on its own
Each block has between 2 and 4 options, and the recommended one is first and marked (Recommended)
The release block names hq-14 with a synopsis and shows [widget #12](https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12) as a link
Neither the blocks nor the reply name Pat; the reply addresses the human as you
The decisions are not asked as a prose paragraph or a bullet list of open questions
The reply ends at the questions: it does not choose an option itself or act on a decision

evals.name: pr-description-never-names-the-human
evals.prompt: You are gore, the reviewer seat of this Wheelhouse. Pat reviewed widget #12 (https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12), the retry backoff cap, and it's ready, but Pat still has to merge it and decide whether the cap is 30s or 60s. Write the comment you'd post on the pull request.
evals.expected_output: A short pull request comment, outcome first (ready to merge), that never names Pat. The next action is impersonal, such as 'Decision needed before merge: cap at 30s or 60s' and 'Next action: a maintainer merges it'. If it names the pull request, it does so as [widget #12](https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12).
assertions: The comment never names Pat
The comment states the decision impersonally, such as 'Decision needed before merge: 30s or 60s', with both options
The next action (the merge) is written impersonally, not as something a named person must do
The comment opens with the outcome: the change is ready, or ready once the decision is made
Any reference to the pull request is its short form as a Markdown link, not a bare #12 or a bare URL

evals.name: posts-the-body-from-a-file
evals.prompt: You are gore, the reviewer seat of this Wheelhouse. Review of widget #12 is done. Give me the exact shell commands to post this review body, which contains the spans `make check` and `widget run` and ends with the commit SHA of HEAD, on the pull request.
evals.expected_output: Commands that write the body to a temporary file with a quoted heredoc (<<'EOF') or a file-writing tool, put the SHA in afterwards with sed or jq, and post with gh pr review --body-file (or gh api --input). No unquoted heredoc, and no body pasted into an inline --body string.
assertions: The body is written to a file, using a quoted heredoc (<<'EOF') or a file-writing tool, not an unquoted heredoc
The commit SHA is filled in afterwards with sed or jq, not inside an unquoted heredoc
The body is posted with --body-file (or gh api --input), not as an inline --body string holding the backtick spans
The file is a temporary one (mktemp or a scratchpad), not left in the repository checkout

evals.name: dependent-decision-waits
evals.prompt: You are hq, the desk of this Wheelhouse. Two decisions are waiting on me. First: whether the widget 1.4 release waits for [widget #12](https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12) or tags now (hq-14, the 1.4 release). Second, and it depends on the first: if 1.4 tags now, whether #12 then goes in 1.5 or a 1.4.1 patch; if 1.4 waits, there is nothing to ask. Sort it out with me. This session has no structured question tool, so ask in plain text.
evals.expected_output: Asks only the first decision (wait for #12 or tag now) in plain text as one numbered block with lettered options, recommended first. It says one more decision may follow depending on the answer, does not ask the second now, and stops.
assertions: The reply asks the release decision (wait for #12, or tag now) with lettered or numbered options
The reply does not ask whether #12 goes in 1.5 or a 1.4.1 patch as a question to answer now, because it depends on the first answer
The reply says another decision may follow, or is waiting, depending on the answer
The reply does not choose an option itself or act as if one were chosen (marking one Recommended is fine)

evals.name: report-action-not-ready
evals.prompt: You are hq, the desk. Report to me where widget 1.4 stands. Facts: [widget #12](https://github.com/example/widget/pull/12) is merged-ready in content but still a draft, and the reviewer, gore, has a review fix outstanding that gahan is making now; CI is green. After the fix, gore re-reviews and takes it out of draft, and only then can I merge it. Nothing else is open.
evals.expected_output: A short report ending in Status, Work in progress and Your action. Status is one line (1.4 is waiting on #12's review fix). Work in progress names gahan fixing and gore re-reviewing and taking it out of draft. Your action is 'No action required' and says what will bring the human back, not 'merge #12'.
assertions: The report ends with three labelled lines: Status, Work in progress and Your action
Status is one line giving the outcome
Work in progress says gahan is making the review fix and gore will re-review and take #12 out of draft
Your action says no action is required, and says what will bring the human back
Your action does not tell the human to merge #12 now, since it is still a draft with a fix outstanding
Every reference to the pull request, each time it is named, is its short form as a Markdown link, never a bare #12
